title: Diverse Critical Interaction Generation for Planning and Planner Evaluation

control_signal.value: A per-vehicle style variable q; its first dimension q(1) sets how critical or conservative the vehicle behaves (swept from -2.0 to 2.0). Also goals and current states of all agents.

control_mechanism.value: Style code fed to a GAN generator along with states and goals; multi-branch safe/critical discriminators and an InfoGAN-style auxiliary distribution network tie the style dimension to behaviour. Generator outputs key waypoints, Bezier-interpolated.

base_model.value: RouteGAN: styled GAN generating key waypoints of a single vehicle, interpolated with Bezier curves, applied iteratively to produce multi-agent interaction.

datasets.value: Argoverse (the modified interaction data used by CMTS: straight road and intersections) and INTERACTION roundabout data, with pseudo-critical interactions created by temporal realignment and local deformation.

metrics.value: Qualitative case studies of generated interactions; collision rate of tested planners (Data, IDM, Astar) against RouteGAN opponents at different q(1).

controllability_evidence.value: Collision rate rises monotonically with q(1): Data planner 4.2% at -2.0 to 95.3% at 2.0; IDM 1.4% to 24.4%; Astar 0.0% to 6.5%.

stated_limitations.value: Collision is not a penalty in the model, so RouteGAN itself is not best for collision avoidance; CMTS noted to fail on roundabouts. Packet gives no dedicated limitations section.

notes: Control family inferred as trained-in style conditioning (GAN with latent style code); the packet does not use that label. Critical data relied on simple augmentation tricks.
